record.paper_title: Open Problems in Hydrodynamical Approach to Relativistic Heavy Ion Collisions
record.context_brief: Freeze-out, continuous emission, and final hadron spectra
record.original_question: How should final hadron spectra be constructed from hydrodynamical solutions of relativistic heavy-ion collisions when the standard Cooper-Frye sudden-freeze-out picture assumes emission from a sharp hypersurface but has conservation, negative-flux, and artificial-entropy-production problems, while continuous-emission models allow broad emission temperatures and can describe the same spectra and flow equally well?

evidence.quote: To analyze the physical observables in terms of the hydrodynamical scenario, we have to construct the particle spectra from the hydro solution.
The Cooper-Frye formula gives the invariant momentum distribution in this case.

Although simple and elegant, this sudden freeze-out is not only an idealization but also contains some problems such as conservation of energy and momentum, negative flux and artificial entropy production.

It should be emphasized that the two extremely cases, a sharp temperature surface of sudden freeze-out and almost flat distribution of temperature of the continuous emission scenario give equally good description of the observed spectra and flow.

artifact.status_search_result: The problem of constructing final hadron spectra from hydrodynamic solutions in a way that avoids the conservation, negative-flux, and artificial-entropy issues of the Cooper-Frye sudden freeze-out remains an active area. Generalized hydro-kinetic and continuous-emission formalisms (Sinyukov et al., Grassi et al.) and self-consistent viscous Cooper-Frye prescriptions (e.g., iS3D module) have been proposed, but the conversion of fluid to particles remains ambiguous, especially in the viscous case, and no single accepted prescription uniquely discriminates between scenarios that fit data equally well.

status_evidence.title: Particle emission in hydrodynamics: a problem needing a solution
status_evidence.snippet: Surveys various mechanisms for particle emission in hydrodynamics, with key issue being negative contributions in Cooper-Frye for sudden freeze out.
status_evidence.claim: The particle-emission problem in hydrodynamics is still treated as one needing a solution.

status_evidence.title: Particlization in fluid dynamical simulations of heavy-ion collisions: iS3D module
status_evidence.snippet: Conversion of fluid to particles, typically done in the Cooper-Frye formalism, is ambiguous for viscous fluids.
status_evidence.claim: Cooper-Frye particlization remains ambiguous for viscous hydrodynamics.

status_evidence.title: Kinetics vs hydrodynamics: generalization of Landau/Cooper-Frye prescription for freeze-out
status_evidence.snippet: Generalized hydro-kinetic prescription showing freeze-out hypersurfaces depend on particle momentum and do not enclose dense matter.
status_evidence.claim: Generalizations of Cooper-Frye have been proposed but freeze-out hypersurfaces are momentum-dependent.
